source.title: Representation Alignment from a Few Paired Data via Distilled Optimal Transport

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether independently trained image and text encoders share geometry that can support alignment without paired supervision, and reports evidence against that in its tested setting. It also evaluates how much retrieval performance is retained after distilling an OT alignment into lightweight encoders.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports extensive retrieval comparisons, hubness results, alternative anchor-based costs, and zero-shot transfer. Those results evaluate alignment methods or their downstream retrieval, rather than measuring natural representational convergence, so they are not included as rows except where they directly test V4 or V7.
record.test_reason: The zero-pair experiments directly test the no-paired-data branch of V4. The structural-term ablation and explicit argument about insufficient shared geometry bear on V7's partial-convergence component. Neither experiment tests convergence with increasing model capability.
record.authors_conclusion: The record largely captures the authors' conclusion. They find near-random zero-pair retrieval and no benefit from a structural GW term, and interpret these as insufficient shared geometry for unsupervised alignment in their setting. Their anchor-relative OT method aligns frozen encoders using a few hundred paired anchors, works without hidden pairing in the remaining pool, and can be distilled into lightweight inductive encoders.
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired anchors to construct anchor-relative coordinates, solves a global entropic OT coupling, and distills it into trained lightweight encoders; it does not measure alignment across increasing model scale or capability.
record.method_sensitivity: In the FGW ablation, retrieval improves as α increases toward the anchor-relative feature-cost term; the structural term never improves retrieval.

fits_no_version.finding: Distilled encoders retain 94%, 96%, and 97% of an anchor-supervised OT teacher's Recall@1, @5, and @10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An anchor-supervised transductive OT alignment can be compressed into inductive projection heads with little retrieval loss relative to that teacher.

record.problems: The claim-relevant zero-pair and FGW results are shown in figures without reported uncertainty; the text only characterizes the zero-pair results as near-random and says the structural term never improves retrieval. Evidence concerns one image-text encoder pair and does not test model scale or capability.
record.rows_left_out: Left out retrieval comparisons among AnchorDOT and competing alignment methods, hubness comparisons, alternative anchor-based costs, zero-shot classification, and zero-shot retrieval (Sections 4, Appendix C.3, C.5.1, and C.5.2). These evaluate method performance or downstream transfer rather than the versions' representational-convergence measures.

untested.parts: No test of whether cross-modal alignment increases as both encoders improve.
No independently initialized same-architecture backbone comparison; experimental seeds do not constitute this test.
No direct low-loss substitution of original model representations, layer stitching, or same-modality interchangeability test. Teacher-retention results do not establish these.
No recurring interpretable feature or circuit analysis.
No comparison of measured natural convergence across similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions. Alignment-method and transfer-performance ablations measure different outcomes.
No direct estimate of alignment completeness or plateau with scale, and no causal test of shared training data or objectives as explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Failure of three alignment algorithms does not prove that every unsupervised map is impossible. V7's original challenges label reverses the evidence: insufficient shared geometry supports its partial-convergence component. Results explicitly declared in rows_left_out are not counted as missing.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no comparison of alignment across models of increasing size or capability.
The study aligns image and text encoders, but does not test whether their alignment rises as both models improve.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations or analysis of shared features or subspaces across seeds.
Tests trained lightweight projection encoders distilled from an OT teacher, not stitching layers, relative representations, or mapping without paired anchors.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits across models.

Alternative alignment costs and distribution transfer are evaluated, but the study does not test whether a measure of representational convergence changes with similarity metric, settings, or input choice.

Tests whether frozen image and text encoders have enough shared intra-modal geometry for zero-pair structural alignment; does not establish why any shared structure exists, or test whether anchor-supervised alignment plateaus or remains incomplete.
